text: The Tide Warden isn't finished. His voice shakes the water in the pipe, and only the summons understand it.
Nib whispers it for Jaeha. The pipes pour the sea into him so he doesn't die, and take everything else.
Then the giant tells them the catch.
Pull the pipes, and he dies within the hour. When the boss dies, the gate closes, with all of them still inside.
Uncle Pyo looks up toward the rim, far above in the dark. Dami grips his arm.
A window opens: harvest the core, worth an estimated forty billion won. No other option available.
Forty billion won, Jaeha thinks. And everyone in here dies with him.
He swipes the window away.
If he ends the Warden now, he tells the eye, the gate closes on everyone in it. Even the engineers.
The hum deepens until the water jumps. Those engineers are the ones who put the pipes in him.
Even them, says Jaeha. Everyone comes back. It's the only rule he has.
The great eye closes. One long breath, and across the pit, the glass wall fogs white.
When it opens again, the anger is gone. Then Jaeha must leave him here. Again.
For now, Jaeha swears. He'll get everyone out, then come back for him. Nib asks if he says that to everyone. Everyone comes back.
The eye softens. The last one who swore that to him wore orange.
Nib translates, then stares at Jaeha, eyes wide.
Jaeha's hand finds the rusted lamp at his belt. That was his hyung.
Four years ago, before the machines, Minseok sat at the giant's feet and talked to him for three days. The Warden never knew his words. But Minseok smiled at him, and scratched the door.
Minseok was not alone at the end. And neither was the Warden.
Jaeha bows his head over the lamp and cries without a sound. So now he's swearing it twice. Once for himself, and once for his hyung.
He wipes his face. They need proof, something nobody can call fake. Then, says Moon Ahin, it needs a face they can't call fake.
She turns her phone on herself, the chained giant behind her. Her name is Moon Ahin. Her grandfather founded Kanghan's core division.
Then she turns the camera on the Warden. This is what it does.
The tanks, her grandfather's seal on every cap.
The stamped chains. The pipes driven into his coral.
Her eyes shine, but not one tear falls.
Then Uncle Pyo limps into frame and pulls off his respirator. Pyo Dongsik, twenty years walking their traps. Put him in it.
One by one, Dami, Woo and Ho bare their faces too. Put them all in it.
Jaeha watches them, and his tired face breaks into pride.
She stops the recording.
Troopers round the pit wall, and the speakers crackle. The asset must not be damaged. Protect the equipment at all costs.
Inside Borro's husk mask, a green glow kindles.
Equipment, Borro repeats. Jaeha reaches for his back. Go on, Borro. Jaeha's got him.
Borro flares into field form, walks up to the Warden's arm and wraps both hands round a pipe as thick as a tree.
And he rips it out with his bare hands. Violet light geysers across the pit, and seawater closes over the wound.
Jaeha carries sixty percent of that strain, on his knees in the water. His shoulder and his nose both bleed.
And for the first time in four years, the Warden breathes easy. His chains slacken.
Borro drops the pipe into the pit and turns. He is not equipment. Neither am I.
Lyra wipes her eyes, grinning. She likes the big one more every day.
In the control room, panic. Drain seven severed, yield down twelve percent. It's tearing up the asset.
The duty chief slams a red button. Seal the rim. Nobody leaves this gate tonight.
A red window: gate rim sealing, twelve minutes. When it hits zero, the only way out is shut.
Four hundred metres up, the steel frame round the rim starts to close like an iris.
It took two hours to come down, Moon Ahin shouts. Jaeha points into the tunnel. The pumps push the water up and out. They go up with it.
The troopers open fire, and Borro plants himself in front of the hatch, shield up.
The crew and the husks pour through, Nib waving them in.
Jaeha looks back at the eye one last time. Go, the Warden tells him. And come back.
Jaeha raises a thumbs-up, the way Minseok used to.
The giant eye closes once, slowly. A nod.
Borro backs in last and swings the hatch shut on the red light.
Inside, an old tide channel climbs into the dark, black water pumped uphill beside a narrow walkway.
Is the video enough, Moon Ahin asks. It's enough if it gets out, says Jaeha. So they get it out.
At the rear, Lyra hears lots of boots coming up behind them.
A trooper's radio blinks.
And Sora's voice comes through. Keep pushing them up. She'll be waiting at the top.
Then the whole tunnel shudders, and a crack runs across the ceiling.
Nib looks up. The seal closing on the rim is shaking the whole gate.
Eleven minutes thirty-one, and a long climb ahead.
And just ahead of them, the ceiling starts to come down.
